prompt: Prompts with long style instructions still give inconsistent tone. The team has 2,000 approved examples and wants the model itself to write that way.
tells: wants the model itself to write that way
why: Training on many examples changes the model's behavior: fine-tuning.
trap: A few examples in the prompt can't carry 2,000.

prompt: Every request carries a 3,000-token prompt of instructions. The team wants the behavior built into the model so prompts can be short.
tells: built into the model so prompts can be short
why: Fine-tuning bakes behavior in, cutting prompt length.
trap: Max tokens limits output, not the prompt.

prompt: A model must turn doctors' shorthand into a strict report format. Hundreds of real examples exist, and prompting alone gets it right 70% of the time.
why: When prompting plateaus and you have many examples, fine-tune.
trap: Few-shot was effectively what got you to 70%.

prompt: A small model fine-tuned on support tickets matches a large model's quality on that one task at a tenth of the cost.
why: Fine-tuning can make a small model good at one narrow task.
trap: The model is small, but the technique that made it good is fine-tuning.

prompt: The team uploads a file of prompt and ideal-response pairs and starts a training job in Foundry.
why: Training jobs on example pairs are fine-tuning.
trap: Examples in a training file aren't in the prompt, so it's not few-shot.

prompt: Better prompts and grounding with data have both been tried, and answers still miss the required style. What is the usual next, most effortful step?
why: The usual order is prompt, then ground, then fine-tune. Fine-tuning takes the most effort.
trap: Prompting and grounding are already done; repeating them won't change the style.

prompt: A model is trained further on a company's past marketing copy so everything it writes sounds on-brand.
tells: trained further on a company's past marketing copy
why: Training further on your own data is fine-tuning.
trap: It's training, not adding examples to a prompt.

prompt: A team has 10,000 labeled emails and wants a generative model trained to reply in their support team's exact style and structure.
tells: trained to reply in their support team's exact style
why: Training a model on many examples of the desired output is fine-tuning.
trap: 10,000 examples won't fit in a prompt, so few-shot is out.
